Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15103 of 2022
Applicant :- Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sikandar B. Kochar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Basant Kumar Chauhan
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and
Mr. Basant Kumar Chauhan, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant/complainant.
By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant- Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu,
who is involved in Case Crime No. 262 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B of I.P.C. and 3/4 of D.
P. Act, Police Station- Alinagar, District- Chandauli, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency
of trial.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
As per prosecution case, in brief, the informant who is father of deceased has lodged an F.I.R. on 04.12.2020 against the present applicant- Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu and other co-accused persons namely, Virendra Chauhan @ Bablu, Vijaya Devi, Prema Devi, Pyarelal Chauhan, who are husband, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, mother-in-law and father-in-law respectively of the deceased Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51282298/
1 with the allegations inter-alia that marriage of his daughter was solemnized on 15.06.2019 with the present applicant and in her marriage, sufficient dowry with an amount of Rs. 3 lacs was given to her in-laws, but there was consistent demand of four wheeler Bolero Car and a gold chain from their side.

entities.text: Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After some time of the marriage, the accused persons started harassing and beating his daughter and she was confined in a room and even they used to restrict her from food, he tried to pacify the matter but they were adamant on their demand and they have threatened the informant that if their demands are not fulfilled, they can go up to any extent.
On 04.12.2020, at around 10 O'clock in the morning, he received information from the Police (no. 112) that his daughter has been strangled to death.

The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that, as per postmortem report, deceased died due to asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging, the hyoid bone was found intact and there was a gap of 4 cm between the knot and ligature mark on the body of the deceased.
It is also submitted that no other injury was found on the body of the deceased, which negate the prosecution case of cruelty soon before death.
Therefore, presumption under Section 113-B shall not be attracted.
Lastly, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

The applicant is languishing in jail since 07.12.2020 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that marriage of the deceased with the applicant was solemnized on 15.06.2019 and she died her unnatural death on 04.12.2020 within short span of 1 year, 5 months and 20 days in her matrimonial home.
It is also pointed out that information about death of the deceased was not given by the applicant or his family members to the informant or any other relatives of the deceased.
The informant received information on 04.12.2020 by the Police and thereafter, he reached the spot and took out the dead body of the deceased after breaking the door.

Thereafter inquest proceeding of the dead body of the deceased was conducted,
but at that time also, neither applicant nor his family members were present there.

Whereas,
informant who is father of the deceased was very much present and after postmortem of the deceased, dead body was received by the informant Munna Chauhan.

In the statement of the informant under Section 161 Cr.P.C., it is also pointed out that, prior to death of the deceased, the informant along with other persons went to the house of the applicant and tried to convince them,
but they were adamant on their demand.
Considering the gravity of offence, the bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find substance in the submission of learned A.G.A. that deceased died her unnatural death within short span of 1 year, 5 months and 20 days in the house of the applicant.

There is no material on record to indicate that any information regarding death of the deceased was given by the applicant to the informant or any other family members/relatives of the deceased, which shows the abnormal conduct with ulterior motive of the applicant.

During investigation, informant and other witnesses have supported the prosecution case, therefore, merely by non-finding of any injury on the body of the deceased, it cannot be said that no cruelty was conducted by the accused persons soon before the Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51282298/
2 death of the deceased.

entities.text: Dhirendra Chauhan @ Chhotu vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I am of the view that cruelty means wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman concerned to commit suicide or cause grave injury to her life, limb or health.
The word "soon before" in Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act can not be limited by fixing time limit.
It is up to the Court to determine the same, depending upon the facts and circumstances of the case.
In view of above, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant is rejected at this stage.
However it is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
